ambient.comment: ADR-0069 D9. Non-interactive, one-shot, decorative motion on a background or ground plane only. MUST NOT be used for a state change, transition, entrance or exit, and MUST NOT be applied to text, a control or any element carrying content. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce it is not played. Single authorised use: the portrait hero's background settle (ADR-0069 D8); a second use needs a new ADR.

orbit.comment: ADR-0098 D5 — the eighth value and the first that is not a one-way duration. Every other entry is the time from one state to another; this is the period of one revolution of BrandBorder rotating edge, which has no destination state. Binding it to a transition duration would tie the speed of a loop to the speed of a hover. 6s is deliberately slow: a fast rotation on a live card reads as an error condition rather than a broadcast. Admissible in exactly two bounded places (hover, live), in neither does it outlive its boundary, and `ambient` is untouched by this addition.

entrance.comment: ADR-0087 D1. The arrival of a row of content below the fold, and nothing else. Every other duration here times a change that interrupts a reader who is waiting for it; an entrance happens to something the reader is already looking at, which is a different kind of time and not a longer one of the same kind. MUST NOT be used above the fold, for an interaction, or for a transition between states. The content it moves is visible before it moves: an entrance is never what makes it visible.

duration.comment: 7 values max (Chapter 3 §3.14, amended by ADR-0069 D9 and ADR-0087 D1) — Chapter 5 §5.6

spring.comment: Reserved for record/medal celebratory moments (L8 §SP.7) only

angle.comment: ADR-0059 §D7. Measured from the four stroke geometries of the identity motif ("نقطة الارتقاء / The Rise", Chapter 1 §2.1): 44.09°, 45.14°, 44.15°, mean 44.46°. Rounded to 45° for an exact 1:1 pixel-grid slope. §D7.1: this vector is brand geometry, NOT reading direction — it MUST NOT mirror under RTL.

offset.comment: Translate magnitude on BOTH axes. Equal x and y is what makes the vector 45° — the angle above is descriptive, this is the value that produces it.

stagger.comment: Chapter 5 §5.7: 40–80ms between elements. 60ms is the midpoint.

stagger-steps.comment: Chapter 5 §5.7 caps total stagger at 600ms; 10 × 60ms is exactly that ceiling. Elements past the tenth reuse the last delay rather than extending the sequence.

scale.comment: ADR-0067. Chapter 5 §5.11 authorises `transform: scale()` as the way to change a surface's apparent size, but fixes no magnitude — this is that magnitude, bounded rather than chosen. A raised card's hover is ONE physical event (it comes toward the reader), so the scale is bounded by the lift it accompanies: `{motion.ascent.offset}` ÷ 4 = 4px (ADR-0066 D3). LOWER BOUND — the edge must move further than `{border.width.default}` (1px), or the growth cannot be resolved as depth at all. UPPER BOUND — the edge must move LESS than the 4px rise, or a card in a row outruns its own lift sideways and the eye reads the row jittering instead of the card rising, which is the exact failure ADR-0066 D3 removed from the diagonal. Edge displacement is width × (scale-1) ÷ 2. Across the full width range the standard covers — 358px (stacked card, 390px viewport) → 1.79px, 294px (contact hero card at xl) → 1.47px, 600px (half of the 1248px panel row, the widest surface `.lift` can reach) → 3.00px — every value sits inside 1px … 4px. Guarded by `surface-standard.spec.ts`.
